title: Indonesia's 2027 wage rise: Can 6-8% increases cost it garment orders?
content:
Indonesia’s 2027 minimum-wage formula could lift provincial rates by about 5.9–8 per cent, creating planning uncertainty for textile and garment exporters.
Under PP 49/2025, provinces apply inflation plus growth multiplied by an alpha of 0.50–0.90, with governors setting final rates.
West Java exporters face the largest pressure, while Central Java may gain a cost edge.

title: Italian textile-machinery orders rise 7%: Can recovery follow in 2027?
content:
ACIMIT reported Italian textile-machinery order intake rose 7 per cent year on year in Q3 2026, but the overall market remained weak.
Export orders grew 8 per cent, domestic orders fell 4 per cent and total orders declined 4 per cent from the previous quarter.
The order index was 44.6, backlog 3.5 months and capacity utilisation fell to 72.4 per cent, with Q4 orders expected stable or lower.

title: Vietnam's $47.5 bn textile target: Can it overcome the US tariff gap?
content:
Vietnam has cut its 2026 textile and garment export goal for a third time, to $47–47.5 billion from about $50 billion at the start of the year.
Exports reached roughly $36 billion in the first nine months, up about 3.3 per cent, while official January–October data show $33.74 billion.
Garment exports rose just 0.7 per cent in Jan–Aug, as other textile categories grew 10.6 per cent.

title: North Indian cotton yarn trade thin, post-Diwali recovery expected
content:
North Indian cotton yarn markets stayed cautious before Diwali, with Ludhiana and Delhi prices steady amid thin trade, weak buying and slow cash flow.
Panipat’s recycled yarn stayed under pressure as festive home textile demand lagged and domestic and export demand remained weak.
Cotton recovered ₹30–50 (~$0.32–0.53) per maund on stronger ICE futures; arrivals totalled 14,000 bales.

title: Bangladesh garment crisis: Is India's $1.46 bn yarn trade at risk?
content:
Bangladesh wage unrest could test India's $1.456 billion cotton-yarn exposure, even as any shift in garment orders to Indian apparel exporters remains unproven.
TexPro shows Bangladesh took 42.85 per cent of India's worldwide cotton-yarn export value in 2025-26, after shipments fell 16.8 per cent.
April-July 2026 exports had recovered 8.5 per cent before factory shutdowns.

title: US cotton futures rebound 1.39% after Democrat’s win
content:
US cotton futures rebounded 1.39 per cent on Wednesday as a weaker dollar and technical buying lifted prices from a nearly one-month low.
The ICE December 2026 contract settled at 78.11 cents per pound, after touching its highest level since October 26.
Faster US harvesting, higher ICE certified stocks, weak grains and a projected 14 per cent drop in India’s cotton output shaped sentiment.

title: Bangladesh garment crisis: Can 690 factories regain buyer confidence?
content:
Bangladesh’s garment sector faces buyer concern after wage protests led nearly 690 factories to suspend production, though many later reopened.
Workers seek a Tk 30,000 (~$241), monthly minimum, up from Tk 12,500; a revised scale is due from December but no amount is agreed.
Exports fell 1.64 per cent in fiscal 2025-26, while TexPro shows pressure in US-bound T-shirts and men’s woven clothing.

title: US' a.k.a. Brands reports 9.7% Q3 sales growth amid rising losses
content:
a.k.a. Brands posted third-quarter net sales of $161.3 million, up 9.7 per cent YoY, as US sales advanced 14 per cent and gross margin widened to 60.1 per cent.
Adjusted EBITDA rose nearly 17 per cent to $8.2 million, although the fashion group’s net loss widened to $7.7 million.
The company narrowed its FY26 sales outlook and reduced its adjusted EBITDA and capital expenditure guidance.
